title: The Shirt That Was Still Damp
scene: On a weekday morning, a favorite blue shirt has not dried overnight. Instead of waiting by the window, the speaker chooses a plain gray shirt and leaves on time.
sceneJa: 平日の朝、着るつもりだった青いシャツが一晩たっても乾いていない。窓辺で待つのをやめ、引き出しの灰色のシャツで間に合わせて予定どおり家を出る。

chunks.ja: 青いシャツが乾いていることを

chunks.en: by the time I got dressed.
But when I lifted it off the drying rack,
chunks.ja: でも物干しから取り上げると

chunks.en: the sleeves were still a little damp.
chunks.ja: 袖はまだ少し湿っていた

chunks.en: I held it up by the window
as if the morning light could finish the job.
chunks.ja: 朝の光が乾かしてくれるとでもいうように

chunks.en: I had better things to do
chunks.ja: ほかにやるべきことがあった
そこで〜で間に合わせた

chunks.en: at the back of my drawer.
chunks.ja: 引き出しの奥にあった

chunks.en: I'd forgotten all about the blue shirt,
chunks.ja: 青いシャツのことなどすっかり忘れていて

chunks.en: which was still hanging by the window.
chunks.ja: それはまだ窓辺に掛かっていた

questions.question: Which split keeps the expression 'count on' together as a meaning unit?
options: I was counting on / my blue shirt being dry / by the time I got dressed.
I was / counting / on my blue shirt being dry by the time I got dressed.
I was counting / on my blue / shirt being dry by the time I got dressed.
questions.explanation: 'I was counting on' expresses reliance or expectation. Keep 'counting on' together before naming what you expected.

questions.question: What does 'I made do with the plain gray one' mean?
options: I sewed a new gray shirt.
I managed with the gray shirt although it wasn't my first choice.
I decided to wait until the blue shirt dried.
questions.explanation: 'Make do with' means to manage using an available, less-preferred substitute.

questions.question: Why does the speaker say 'I had better things to do than wait for a shirt'?
options: They need to buy more clothes immediately.
They are criticizing the person who did the laundry.
They realize waiting would waste time, so they choose another shirt.
questions.explanation: The speaker gently laughs at their own unnecessary waiting and moves on.

speak: Imagine: your favorite item of clothing is not ready when you need it. Read: notice the small shift from frustration to practical amusement. Chunk: read 'I was counting on', 'still a little damp', and 'made do with' as units. Understand: expectation, an inconvenient condition, and a workable substitute. Check: answer all three questions. Speak (30 seconds): describe something you were counting on, what went wrong, and what you made do with instead. Final Read: reread all six sentences without Japanese; lightly stress 'still' and pause after 'On second thought'.
review: New: 'I was counting on ...'（〜を当てにしていた）, 'still a little damp'（まだ少し湿っている）, 'make do with ...'（〜で間に合わせる）. Reuse Lesson 103 'On second thought'（考え直すと）and Lesson 100/103 'By the time ...'（〜する頃には）in a laundry problem rather than a plant or phone habit. The previous 14 lessons included music, race, food, shopping, and plans; this lesson focuses on a mundane material constraint and a low-stakes substitution.
